items.question: Does writing a status accept variants such as other casing or surrounding whitespace, or only the exact enum spelling?
items.chose: writeStatus accepts only an exact, case-sensitive match and does not normalise the input.
items.instead: Normalise the input first (trim, lowercase) and write the canonical status.

items.question: What happens when writeStatus gets a value that is not a status?
items.chose: Throws an Error whose message contains the JSON-quoted value.
items.instead: Return null or a result object, or coerce the value to a default status such as draft.

items.question: Is an old spelling such as 'in-review' accepted on write?
items.chose: Rejects old spellings on write, so only readStatus maps them.
items.instead: Map old spellings to their enum value on write.

items.question: What does readStatus return for a stored value that is not a known status?
items.ticket: Existing values are normalised when read
items.instead: Throw an error, or return the cleaned or original string, or fall back to a default such as draft.

items.question: Which old spellings are mapped to enum values?
items.ticket: Sandbox status is stored as free text (draft, Draft, in-review...)
items.chose: Maps only 'in review' (after cleaning) to review. Any other legacy spelling, such as 'in progress' or 'done', reads as null.
items.instead: Add more aliases (for example 'approved' or 'pending review'), or accept prefix and fuzzy matches.

items.question: How are case, whitespace and separators handled when reading?
items.ticket: Existing values are normalised when read
items.chose: Lowercases, trims, and collapses runs of whitespace, '-' and '_' into one space. Leading and trailing separators are dropped, so '-draft-' reads as draft.
items.instead: Only trim and lowercase, treating '-' and '_' as significant. Alternatively, collapse separators to a hyphen or underscore.

items.question: What does reading an empty or whitespace-only value return?
items.chose: Returns null, since the cleaned string matches no status.
items.instead: Treat it as a default status such as draft, or throw.

items.question: Do inherited object keys such as 'constructor' or '__proto__' read as statuses?
items.chose: Looks values up in Maps so these keys return null.
items.instead: Use a plain object lookup, or a Set, with no special guard.

items.question: How does the batch read treat rows with unreadable statuses?
items.chose: Keeps every row in order with status null and does not throw.
items.instead: Drop unreadable rows, or throw on the first one.

items.question: How are unreadable values reported by the batch read: which form, how duplicates are handled, and in what order?
items.chose: Reports the original stored strings, deduplicated by exact stored form (so 'Unknown' and 'unknown' are separate) and sorted with the default sort.
items.instead: Report the cleaned form, or return row ids, or keep duplicates in first-seen order.

items.question: Does the batch read return an empty result for empty input?
items.chose: Returns empty rows and an empty unreadable list.
items.instead: Throw on empty input, or return null.
